cards.explanation: The answer is glad. David says, “I was glad when they said to me…” and then he gives the invitation: “Let us go to the house of the LORD.” Nobody had to drag him there. I think that's the kind of gladness you can see from across the room, friends, like a baker when the oven timer dings on a good batch.
The answer is the gates of Jerusalem. David says, "Our feet are standing in your gates, O Jerusalem." They had made it all the way there. I bet those feet were happy to stop walking for a second.

The answer is False. David says, "Jerusalem is built up as a city united together…" So the city is joined up, not split apart. A cookie broken in half is a sad thing, friends, but that's not this city.

The answer is True. David says the tribes go up “…to give thanks to the name of the LORD.” That's the reason the song gives for the trip. They go to give thanks, and I think that's a good reason to travel.

The answer is judgment. David says, "For there the thrones of judgment stand, the thrones of the house of David." These are thrones tied to David's house. Sit in one of those, friends, and you'd better know what you're doing.
The answer is the peace of Jerusalem. David says, "Pray for the peace of Jerusalem…" That's the instruction, short and clear. Some instructions come with forty steps, and this one has a single line.
The answer is True. The prayer goes, “May those who love you prosper.” Those words are for the ones who love Jerusalem. Me, I'd be standing there saying, “uh… good stuff… amen.”

The answer is for the sake of his brothers and friends. That's the reason David gives: “For the sake of my brothers and friends, I will say…” and the words he'll say are “Peace be within you.” It's all for them. I bet that lands warmer than any “talk to you later.”

The answer is house. David ends with, “For the sake of the house of the LORD our God, I will seek your prosperity.” The song began with the house of the LORD in verse 1 and finishes there too. That's like walking a loop around the block, friends, and ending up back at your own front door.
